newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Frustration on SAfrica JSE as system freezes trade.
newsitem.headline: Frustration on SAfrica JSE as system freezes trade.

text.p: Frustration gripped the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on Wednesday morning as problems with its electronic trading system for the third consecutive day halted dealings on the South African bourse.

The exchange has lost more than a day's business since the beginning of the week after the Johannesburg Equities Trading System (JET) began experiencing response problems on Monday following the installation of new software at the weekend.
Roy Andersen, the JSE president, told Reuters the delays were unacceptable.
"Yes, it is not acceptable to be delayed in the performance of the market," Andersen said.
On Wednesday the market opened almost two and a half hours late after a series of tests on the system, but trade was halted again shortrly afterwards for further tests.
On Monday some four hours was lost and on Tuesday the opening was delayed for an hour.
"Overseas and institutional frustration is very evident. This is ridiculous," a dealer said.
A trading day is six and a half hours long running from 0730 GMT to 1400 GMT.

Other traders said a substantial amount of money had been lost due to the loss of more than seven hours of trade in total. On average around 450 million rands worth of trade passes through the JSE on every day.
"We are losing a lot of business. Especially with December such a short month with all the holidays, we need to make it up in this period," one said.
Andersen said the JET system, which has been operational since March when the market moved from open outcry to electronic trade, was extensively tested before it was implemented.
"The Chicago exchange tested it fully before we implemented it. My understanding is that it is not unusual to experience (software) problems of this nature," he said.
"We and the Chicago exchange are striving to ensure a 100 percent up-time," he added.
The JET system has failed on at least three occasions since March, the last occasion being at the beginning of September following a network problem.
